title: Living or non-living?
hook: Living things eat, breathe, grow and have babies. A teddy bear does none of these.

intro.say: Living things eat or drink. They breathe. They grow. And they have babies.

story.text: A cat eats, breathes and grows. Living!
story.say: A cat eats. It breathes. It grows. It has kittens. A cat is living!

story.text: A teddy bear does not eat or grow. Non-living.
story.say: A teddy bear does not eat. It does not breathe. It does not grow. A teddy bear is non-living.

story.text: A plant cannot walk, but it drinks and grows. Living!
story.say: A plant cannot walk. But it drinks water, it breathes, and it grows. A plant is living!

story.text: A toy robot moves, but it does not eat or grow. Non-living.
story.say: A toy robot can move. But it does not eat, breathe or grow. A robot is non-living.

atHome.thing: A walk downstairs or in the park
atHome.ask: Point at 5 things: “Living or non-living? How do you know?”
Water it together for a week. “Is it growing? Then it is living.”
“It moves. Does it eat? Does it grow? So is it living?”

tips: Moving is not the test. Cars and robots move but are non-living; plants do not walk but are living.
Use the four questions every time: Does it eat or drink? Breathe? Grow? Have babies?
